subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle as an armored interceptor van, keeping the rig simple with just a few joints like chassis root, turret yaw, and cannon pitch rather than a full creature-style skeleton.

Sizing it at roughly 5.2m long, 2.3m wide, 2.2m tall with four large wheels, and planning to build the boxy wedge body using an extruded side profile defined by a set of outline points from rear to front, giving it the hood, windshield, and sloped hull shape. Thinking through paint as a dark navy countershade, and considering pulling in existing kit components like clockwork panelled metal pieces, though that carries some API risk I want to keep in check.

I decide to roll my own paints instead and pull from a glow kit for materials. Laying out the hull extrusion width, placing the four cylindrical wheels with their axes rotated to run along x, positioning them at the front and rear with slight protrusion beyond the hull for an armored look, and adding thin box fenders over each wheel; also planning a slanted, tinted glass windshield with a subtle cyan emissive glow.

Working out the windshield box's tilt angle and placement...

Placing it offset along the hull normal at the midpoint of the windshield line, then adding dark glass side windows with cyan glow edges, a glowing roof light bar, and magenta/cyan neon trim along the sill and hood.

Now I'm adding a bull bar bumper with a glowing grille texture, boxy headlights glowing white-cyan, and a corporate decal on the door panel -- a hexagon emblem with "NOVACORP RIOT CONTROL" text in magenta and yellow, textured as a front-facing plane on each side.

Now I'm designing the roof-mounted water cannon turret: a yaw joint with base cylinder and dome, a pitch joint for the barrel with a muzzle flare ring, and placing the water tank as a horizontal cylinder behind the cab with a glowing level window. I'm working out rough coordinates for the turret, tank, and light bar positions along the roof.

Setting up the joint hierarchy now: a chassis root joint, a turret joint parented to it, and a pitch joint for the cannon positioned near the light bar, with the barrel parts attached along a normalized direction vector pointing slightly upward and forward.

Now I'm planning the wheel assemblies—each wheel gets its own joint parented to the chassis, rotated along the x-axis, with a dark tire cylinder, a steel rim cylinder, and a glowing magenta torus ring for accent, plus a small hub cap at the center.

I'm also detailing exterior features: window cage bars, rear door lines, a red rear light bar, roof rack, cameras, side steps, a front ram wedge push bar, exhaust vents, a front license plate, and hood signage reading "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT." I'm settling on the color palette—gunmetal base, magenta and cyan accents, yellow highlights, and a white stripe panel for the custom paint job.

For the paint function, I'm working out a cyberpunk two-tone scheme: grimy dark lower panels, pale off-white upper panels, with a magenta neon stripe along the side using noise and smoothstep utilities from the SDK, applied in model coordinates after the hull extrusion.

Now I'm placing the cabin glass -- a windscreen and side window boxes set slightly outside the hull surface with beveled rims, plus vertical grille bars spaced across each side window, before adding a decal logo plane.

Now I'm adding the rear door seam and taillight strip details, plus a magenta underglow plate beneath the hull between the wheels, and cyan neon rods tracing the hood edge using joint-based rod geometry.

Writing helper functions...

Adding alternating red/blue strobe modules on the light bar, then placing a roof-mounted water tank with domed end caps, retaining straps, and a glowing level window on the side.

Connecting the tank to the turret with a steel support rod, then building the turret itself: a pedestal cylinder, a yaw-rotating head box, and a pitch-pivoting cannon barrel mount.

Now I'm detailing the barrel with a flaring nozzle, glowing muzzle ring, and banded outer sleeve, plus adding a side camera/optic housing, mirrors with arms, whip antennas, a sensor mast with a glowing tip, and sirens — thinking through small details like vents, a hood decal, and roof lettering to round out the vehicle.

Now I'm figuring out the hazard-stripe ram plate on the front bumper and positioning the four wheels, then considering fender flares to cover the part of the wheels buried in the hull, likely using simple boxes as flares for simplicity.

I'm also sketching a side step plank sized to fit between the front and rear wheels, with a glowing magenta neon strip on its edge, plus flat decal-style boxes for pale side stripes over the existing panel paint.

Now I'm placing decal text on the rear doors, something like diagonal "ORDER" chevrons or "COMPLIANCE IS MANDATORY" lettering, and working out the orientation vectors so the plane faces correctly when viewed from behind the vehicle.

I'll trust the plane orientation works with default up-axis conventions and move on to planning the textures needed: logo side panel, grille, hazard markings, rear text, and a windshield sticker reading "RIOT CTRL", aiming for around 400 lines of code with standard materials handling the glow effects fine.

Now I'm setting up the builder with a chassis joint, defining helper functions for boxes and glowing neon rods bound to the chassis, and making sure glow effects work correctly with painted colors rather than throwing errors.

Then I'm defining the hull shape as an extruded outline along the chassis, checking the polygon points don't self-intersect, and writing a paint function that shades the hull with noise-based color mixing depending on height.

I'm adding seam lines, a magenta stripe band, grime darkening near the bottom, and subtle lightening on upward-facing surfaces, making sure the function returns a valid color type for the paint API.

Next I'm setting up wheel joints for all four corners, mirroring left/right with a sign flag and distinguishing front/rear positions, aligning cylinder and torus parts along the x-axis for the wheel bone structure.

Still designing wheel details...

Adding more details...

Still working out cannon geometry...

Adding a flared muzzle with a glowing cyan disc at the tip, then moving on to extra hull details like the bull bar, door handles, and roof lightbar accents.

I'm planning neon rod placement along the roofline in magenta and yellow plus vertical cyan strips near the A-pillar, then sketching out the logo texture — a hexagon emblem with "VANTAGE" lettering, a smaller "CIVIL ORDER DIVISION" subtitle, and a yellow chevron bar on a transparent background with a dark panel rect behind it.

I'm also designing the grille texture with cyan slit lines, a hazard-stripe pattern in yellow/black, a rear panel with "COMPLY OR BE WASHED AWAY" text sized via textLength, and a small license plate graphic reading "NC-4471-RIOT." Now I'm working out exact placement for the grille texture on the tilted front hull face, figuring the right z/y offset and size to match the hull's slight forward tilt.

I'm adjusting bumper and headlight positions to avoid overlaps—lowering the bumper, narrowing the grille width, and shifting headlights outward slightly so everything fits cleanly on the front face without colliding.
